hooks.prompt: Check if this turn made significant code changes (new features, architecture changes, discovered gotchas). If so, briefly suggest the user run /revise-claude-md to capture learnings in CLAUDE.md. Only suggest if meaningful patterns were discovered. Do not suggest for trivial changes, and do not repeat if already suggested this session.
This session is ending. If significant codebase changes were made and CLAUDE.md was not updated, remind the user to run /revise-claude-md in their next session to capture learnings.

council_tool.title: Council as a tool

heads_up.title: Heads-up side-check
heads_up.description: Experimental: applies only when Claude Code runs with CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_FUNCTION_HOOKS=1. While Claude works a long turn, one council seat, codex by default, rereads the last five turns and the last eight tool results and may show one line above the prompt. manifest.description: Production-ready Claude Code hooks, each installable on its own as a plugin.

plugins.name: context-hogs
plugins.description: Per-file context-cost leaderboard: attributes every tool result's tokens to the files it loaded, so you know which files cost you the most.

plugins.name: cache-tax
plugins.description: The comeback price of a cold prompt cache, shown before you pay it: a UserPromptSubmit guard that warns (or refuses once) when your next message re-writes a lapsed 1-hour cache at up to 80x the read rate, a SessionStart hook that prices a stale resume, and a one-line status line segment with minutes left and the cold-comeback cost.

plugins.name: nerf-receipts
plugins.description: A personal flight recorder for Claude Code quality: records your own per-session failure rate, edit churn, and tokens/task by model version, and flags real shifts when a model changes.

plugins.name: dead-rules-audit
plugins.description: CLAUDE.md compliance scorecard: tallies which rules Claude actually follows vs ignores as you edit, and flags chronically-ignored rules to promote into a deterministic hook.

plugins.name: pr-provenance-stamp
plugins.description: Stamps a provenance receipt (prompts, estimated spend, tests run with exit codes, and a truthful agent-authored line split) into your PR body on `gh pr create`.

plugins.name: standup-autopilot
plugins.description: Writes your daily standup from what your agents actually did across repos: captures tasks, tests, PRs, and blockers from session transcripts and re-injects yesterday's open blockers next session.

plugins.name: dead-end-registry
plugins.description: Remembers approaches you tried and reverted (with reason and estimated token cost) and warns before you retry them, via a prompt-submit card and an ask-before-edit guard.

plugins.name: bounty-board
plugins.description: Prices your repo's TODO/FIXME/HACK debt as aging XP bounties, injects the top 3 as opportunistic side quests, and verifies + pays out bounties you genuinely clear.

plugins.name: block-dangerous-commands
plugins.description: PreToolUse guard for Bash: blocks dangerous shell commands (rm -rf ~, fork bombs, curl|sh, force push to main) before they run, with three safety levels and opt-in per-level ask mode.

plugins.name: protect-secrets
plugins.description: Secrets firewall for tool calls: denies (or asks, per level) any Read/Edit/Write/Bash/Grep that would read, search, modify, or exfiltrate .env files, SSH keys, cloud credentials, or keystores, with tiered safety levels tunable via HOOK_SAFETY_LEVEL.

plugins.name: git-safety
plugins.description: Branch-aware git guardrails plus destructive gh CLI protection: denies pushes to main/master, protected-branch deletion, direct commit/merge/rebase/reset/push on a protected branch, and gh pr merge/close, issue close, release and repo delete.

plugins.name: protect-tests
plugins.description: Stops "fake green" test-gaming: blocks the agent from deleting, renaming-away, or skip/xfail-disabling tests so it fixes the code instead, across pytest, jest, Go, JUnit, RSpec, and more.

plugins.name: case-insensitive-guard
plugins.description: Stops `rm -rf content` destroying `Content` on case-insensitive filesystems (APFS/exFAT/NTFS): resolves the real target of destructive commands through cd chains, quotes, and subshells, and denies provable case collisions.

plugins.name: config-guard
plugins.description: Who guards the guards: blocks the agent from tampering with its own guardrail config (settings.json, hook scripts, hooks.json, .mcp.json, plugin manifests, claude CLI config writes); reads always pass.

plugins.name: subagent-spawn-cap
plugins.description: Per-session subagent spawn budget: a PreToolUse guard on the Agent tool that counts every spawn (nested fan-outs included) in an append-only ledger, asks at SPAWN_CAP_ASK (default 20) and every SPAWN_CAP_ASK_STEP after it (default 10), and denies at SPAWN_CAP_DENY (default 60). The total cap Claude Code 2.1.224 removed, back under the user's control.

plugins.name: config-watch
plugins.description: Tripwire for out-of-band config changes: warns on every mid-session settings/skills change (or blocks it with CONFIG_WATCH_BLOCK=true) to catch installer scripts and npm payloads rewriting settings behind Claude Code's back.

plugins.name: auto-stage
plugins.description: Automatic git staging: runs `git add` on every file Claude edits or writes, so `git status` always shows exactly what Claude touched and pre-commit review needs no manual staging.

plugins.name: format-code
plugins.description: Auto-formats files the moment Claude writes them: ruff for Python, prettier for JS/TS/JSON/MD/YAML/HTML, with shell-injection-safe argv execution and silent skips for everything else.

plugins.name: session-logger
plugins.description: Durable markdown log of every session (cwd, git repo, files touched, secret-redacted bash commands), appended async so logging never blocks Claude.

plugins.name: instructions-audit
plugins.description: Prompt-injection tripwire for CLAUDE.md and .claude/rules files: flags invisible-Unicode smuggling, secret read/exfil directives, curl|sh, decode-and-execute, and hook/settings tampering as instructions load, then locks the session (every prompt and tool call denied) until a human clears it.

plugins.name: notify-permission
plugins.description: Slack alerts when Claude Code needs you: posts a rich card (project, session, and what needs approval) to your webhook on permission, idle, and choice prompts.

plugins.name: guard-pack
plugins.description: All seven guard hooks in one Node process: subagent-spawn-cap, config-guard, block-dangerous-commands, protect-secrets, protect-tests, git-safety, and case-insensitive-guard, first blocking verdict wins. One ~35 ms Node startup per tool call instead of seven. Do not install alongside the individual guard plugins.

name: antigravity
description: Claude Code plugin: run the Antigravity CLI (Gemini) as a collaborating sub-agent with intelligent model routing across the SDLC. Community project; not affiliated with Google/Anthropic.

manifest.name: antigravity
manifest.description: Run the Antigravity CLI (Gemini) as a collaborating AI inside Claude Code, with intelligent model routing across the SDLC. Claude conducts — requirements, architecture, the hard 20%, verification, review — and routes deterministic, high-volume work (scaffolding, tests, first-pass review, migrations, web/Vertex AI Search) to Antigravity. Hybrid agentic engineering; lower token cost as a financial lever.

default_tier.title: Default Antigravity tier
default_tier.description: Tier used by agy-delegate.sh when --tier is not passed. One of: flash (Gemini 3.8 Flash High, default — bulk work), flash-lo (Flash Low, cheapest/trivial), pro (Gemini 4 Argon High, harder reasoning).

timeout.title: Default delegation timeout
timeout.description: Default agy print-mode timeout when --timeout is not passed, e.g. 5m, 10m, 300s.

coding_policy.title: Inject routing policy at session start
coding_policy.description: When on, a SessionStart hook injects this plugin's cost-aware routing policy (delegate above the break-even, keep Claude's context lean, always verify agy's output) as session context, so the discipline applies without invoking the skill. Set to off/false/0/no to suppress.

default_model.title: Default executor model (exact agy model name)
default_model.description: agy is multi-model. Set an exact model name from `agy models` (e.g. a Claude/GPT model on plans that expose them) to use as the executor when --tier/--model are not passed. Leave empty to use the tier mapping (Gemini by default). The 'Claude conducts, a different/cheaper model executes' design gives the cost + cross-model-verification benefit, so a non-Claude executor is recommended.

tier_flash.title: Model for the 'flash' tier
tier_flash.description: Override the exact agy model the 'flash' tier maps to (default: Gemini 3.8 Flash (High)). Use a name from `agy models`.

tier_flash_lo.title: Model for the 'flash-lo' tier
tier_flash_lo.description: Override the exact agy model the 'flash-lo' tier maps to (default: Gemini 3.8 Flash (Low)). Use a name from `agy models`.

tier_pro.title: Model for the 'pro' tier
tier_pro.description: Override the exact agy model the 'pro' tier maps to (default: Gemini 4 Argon (High)). Use a name from `agy models`.

structured_output.title: Use agy's structured JSON output
structured_output.description: When on (default), agy-delegate runs agy with --output-format json (agy >= 1.1.8, requires python3) to classify failures from the structured error and report token usage as an AGY_USAGE line on stderr. The text on stdout is unchanged. Set to off/false/0/no to force the plain-text path.

digest_warn_chars.title: Digest-size warning threshold (chars)
digest_warn_chars.description: agy-delegate warns on stderr when a reply exceeds this many characters — a raw dump instead of the digest the cost discipline calls for. Empty = 8000. Set 0 to disable.

delegation_nudge.title: Nudge delegation on bulk-looking prompts
delegation_nudge.description: When on, a UserPromptSubmit hook adds a short advisory note to Claude's context when a prompt looks like bulk work above the delegation break-even (mass edits, migrations, exhaustive tests, fan-out search). Advisory only — Claude still makes the break-even judgment per task. Set to off/false/0/no to suppress.

usage_log.title: Cost-measurement log file (AGY_USAGE / AGY_SIGNAL)
usage_log.description: Absolute path. When set, every delegation appends its AGY_USAGE (token counts) and AGY_SIGNAL (failure) line to this file in addition to stderr. Use this whenever you are MEASURING cost: stderr is easily lost — piping the wrapper through `2>&1 | tail -N` to keep Claude's context lean keeps the digest and silently drops the usage line, which makes the Gemini side look cheaper than it is. Env AGY_USAGE_LOG overrides this. Empty = off.

name: sloptrim
description: A local detector for AI-writing patterns. Scores every prose file your agent saves. Python standard library only, no network, no model.

manifest.name: sloptrim
manifest.description: Scores the first 262,144 characters of extracted prose from files accepted up to 512 KB for plain text and 4 MB for supported archives, against a catalogue of 71 documented patterns, 62 of them with a detector behind them and 50 able to move the score. It names the ones that fired so the flagged spans get fixed before the file ships. The 0 to 100 score lands in one of five bands: clean, light tells, mixed, heavy tells, pervasive tells. Every band describes the prose and none of them names an author. Reads 20 formats including .docx and .epub. Deterministic, Python standard library only, no network, no model. Prose only; code, config and commits stay untouched.

metadata.description: Han: evidence-based planning, investigation, and documentation skills for software projects.

plugins.name: han
plugins.description: Meta-plugin that installs the bundled Han suite. Has no components of its own; it depends on han-communication, han-core, han-documentation, han-research, han-planning, han-coding, han-github, and han-reporting so installing it pulls them all in. Does not bundle the opt-in han-feedback, han-atlassian, or han-plugin-builder plugins.

plugins.name: han-communication
plugins.description: Foundational communication plugin for the Han suite. Owns the canonical readability standard, writing-voice profile, and explanation standard, the readability-guidance skill that surfaces the first two into a calling skill's context for in-voice drafting, the explanation-guidance skill that surfaces the third at the point a run talks to a person, the readability-editor agent that runs the adversarial rewrite, and the edit-for-readability skill. Depends on nothing and sits beneath every other plugin; the plugins that produce prose output depend on it.

plugins.name: han-core
plugins.description: The shared foundation of the Han suite: the specialist agent roster the other plugins dispatch, the project-discovery skill with its project-scanner agent, and the canonical evidence and YAGNI rule files. The documentation skills live in han-documentation, the pre-planning research skills in han-research, the planning skills in han-planning, and the coding skills in han-coding; each depends on han-core.

plugins.name: han-documentation
plugins.description: Documentation skills for the Han suite: writing down what the team built and decided. Home of project-documentation, architectural-decision-record, and runbook. Depends on han-communication and han-core; bundled by the han meta-plugin.

plugins.name: han-research
plugins.description: Pre-planning knowledge-work skills for the Han suite: understanding a problem before anyone commits to a plan. Home of research, gap-analysis, and issue-triage, plus the research-analyst agent. Depends on han-communication and han-core; bundled by the han meta-plugin.

plugins.name: han-planning
plugins.description: Planning skills for the Han suite: specifying, planning, sequencing, breaking down, and stress-testing work before implementation. Home of plan-a-feature, plan-implementation, plan-a-phased-build, plan-work-items, and iterative-plan-review, plus the discussion-facilitator agent. Depends on han-communication and han-core; bundled by the han meta-plugin.

plugins.name: han-coding
plugins.description: Code-writing and execution skills for the Han suite. Home of the tdd skill, which drives a feature or behavior through a BDD-framed red-green-refactor loop with an enforced observed-failure gate. Depends on han-core and han-communication; bundled by the han meta-plugin.

plugins.name: han-github
plugins.description: GitHub-specific extensions to Han. Provides skills to post code reviews as PR comments, update a PR description with a consistent format, and other GitHub-facing workflows.

plugins.name: han-reporting
plugins.description: Reporting and summary skills for the Han suite. Turns feature specifications into plain-language stakeholder summaries (also called executive or business summaries) with diagrams, for sharing with non-technical stakeholders before implementation kicks off.

plugins.name: han-feedback
plugins.description: Post-session feedback skill for the Han suite. Captures structured observations, ratings, and improvement ideas on the Han skills you ran in a session and optionally posts them as a GitHub issue to testdouble/han. Opt-in: installed on its own, not pulled in by the han meta-plugin.

plugins.name: han-atlassian
plugins.description: Atlassian-facing extensions to the Han suite. Adds markdown-to-confluence, which publishes a local Markdown file to a user-specified Confluence page; project-documentation-to-confluence, which runs the han-documentation project-documentation skill and then publishes the result there; investigate-to-confluence, which runs the core investigate skill and publishes the resulting investigation report there; code-overview-to-confluence, which runs the core code-overview skill and publishes the resulting overview there; plan-a-feature-to-confluence, which runs the core plan-a-feature skill and publishes the spec and its companion artifacts there as a page tree; and work-items-to-jira, which creates one Jira ticket per slice from a work-items file. All work through the Atlassian MCP server. Depends on han-core, han-documentation, han-planning, and han-coding (its wrapper skills run skills from each and its wrapped skills dispatch the shared han-core agents), and on han-communication (its wrapped prose-producing skills source the shared readability standard), and requires a configured Atlassian MCP server. Opt-in: installed on its own, not pulled in by the han meta-plugin.

plugins.name: han-linear
plugins.description: Linear-facing extensions to the Han suite. Adds work-items-to-linear, which creates one Linear issue per slice from a work-items file. Works through the Linear MCP server and requires it to be configured. Depends on no other Han plugin. Opt-in: installed on its own, not pulled in by the han meta-plugin.

plugins.name: han-ddd
plugins.description: Strategic Domain-Driven Design analysis for the Han suite. Discovers domain boundaries, identifies bounded context candidates (strongly expressed, latent, and speculative), finds boundary leaks, and produces an evidence-backed domain and context map for an existing codebase. Depends on han-communication and han-core. Opt-in: not bundled by the han meta-plugin.

plugins.name: han-plugin-builder
plugins.description: Guidance for building Claude Code skills, agents, and plugins. The guidance skill answers authoring questions and, run with init, vendors the full guidance set into a repo as a path-scoped rule index so the right guidance surfaces while editing skill and agent files. Opt-in and dependency-free: installed on its own, not pulled in by the han meta-plugin.

voice.title: Default narration voice

max_workers.title: CPU limit (0 = automatic)

sound.title: Sound when a long job finishes

mode.title: Review mode (quality or lean)
mode.description: quality (used when this is empty): every finished video gets the full review, with looks, qa and a critic round before delivery. lean: a cheaper draft pass with one look per stage and no critic round unless the video is publish-bound or you ask. Leave empty to use `showtime config mode` (quality unless set there). SHOWTIME_MODE overrides it.

manifest.name: effortless
manifest.description: Sets the reasoning effort for every prompt automatically, shows it under the prompt box, and counts down how long the prompt cache stays warm.

judge.title: Judge
judge.description: Haiku (your own Claude login, no key) always judges handoffs and, unless Jev answers, the effort. auto: Jev as well when a TypeSafe key is set. haiku: Haiku only. jev: Jev as well, and its key may also come from ~/.config/jev/.env.

typesafeKey.title: TypeSafe API key (optional, only for jev)
typesafeKey.description: For the jev judge. Stored as a secret by Claude Code. Left empty, TYPESAFE_API_KEY is used, and with judge set to jev also ~/.config/jev/.env.

handoffSkill.title: Handoff skill (optional)
handoffSkill.description: A skill or slash command that writes the Full handoff, e.g. session-handoff. Empty: effortless writes it itself (checks git, saves HANDOFF.md). Quick is always a fast fork with the built-in prompt.

handoffAfter.title: After a handoff (first choice)
handoffAfter.description: What the handoff bar starts on; it then remembers your last choice. continue: clear and carry on. confirm: clear, the new chat says where things stand and waits. copy: keep the chat and copy the handoff.

effortBias.title: Effort slider
effortBias.description: -2 cheaper to 2 smarter. Tips the judge's close calls that way; sure calls stay. 0: as the judge says.

effortFloor.title: Never below
effortFloor.description: Auto never picks a lower effort than this.

effortCeiling.title: Never above
effortCeiling.description: Auto never picks a higher effort than this.

hide.title: Switched off
hide.description: Comma-separated: handoff (the footer button), timer (the cache countdown), reason (the judge's line), swamp (the context alert), hot (the running-low alert), cold (the cold-cache alert). Empty shows everything. The judge's line is off unless switched on.

modelAuto.title: Cheaper model when it can (experimental)
modelAuto.description: on: a prompt the judge calls simple may run on a cheaper model (Haiku 5.5 or Sonnet), never above the chat's own, when the switch pays. It rarely does in a chat that is in use: the other model rereads the whole chat. off (default): every prompt runs on the chat's model.

helpers.title: Effort for helpers
helpers.description: on: every subagent (helper) the chat sends off gets an effort picked by the judge before it starts, so a quick search runs at low instead of the chat's effort. off (default): helpers run at the chat's effort.

handoffButton.title: Handoff button
handoffButton.description: advised: the button is Compact, and turns into a glowing Handoff when Haiku says a fresh chat would pay off. always: the button is always Handoff.

compactWith.title: Compact with
compactWith.description: haiku: Haiku 5.5 writes the summary when the chat is compacted (far cheaper). session: the chat's own model, as Claude Code does it.

swampAt.title: Swamped at
swampAt.description: The swamp band shows once the context fills this percent of the window.

appearance.title: Appearance
appearance.description: auto: light panels when Claude Code's theme is light, dark otherwise. dark and light fix it.

theme.title: Theme
theme.description: The accent colour of everything effortless draws. violet: the brand colour. orange: Claude Code orange. rose: cherry-blossom pink, with falling petals.

layout.title: Look
layout.description: default: a dashboard band above the prompt (effort, Auto, cache, context, handoff). minimal: small buttons in the footer, no band.

Load this skill BEFORE writing or changing anything that lives in a Postgres database: creating or altering tables and columns (including choosing column types), schema design, migrations and declarative schema files, RLS policies and the tests that verify them, indexes, triggers, database functions, queues and scheduled jobs (pg_cron, pgmq), vector/semantic search (pgvector), and restoring dumps (pg_restore) or importing data. manifest.name: agentic-sop-to-work
manifest.description: Loop Engineering for Claude Code agent loops — deterministic bounded termination (stall + budget), observable health, and bounded state — and Graph Engineering for when one loop isn't enough: typed handoff edges, unique field ownership, bounded back-edges, and static topology validation. Ships agentic-sop-kit (human SOP → controlled loop or bounded graph) plus cross-domain review companions: Second Opinion (honesty reviewer), alcoa-guard (ALCOA+ data-integrity), plugin-forge (plugin linter/scaffolder).

plugins.name: agentic-sop-kit
plugins.description: Human SOP → a controlled agentic loop, or a bounded graph of them: typed handoff edges, one declaring writer per state field, bounded back-edges, and a static topology gate that refuses an illegal graph before it runs. Methodology skills + /sop-flow + a project-scoped regression Stop-hook + the portable kit.

plugins.name: second-opinion-honesty
plugins.description: Independent adversarial honesty reviewer: scrutinizes a DRAFT output's claims-vs-evidence (no fabrication / overreach / invented IDs) before a human approves. Snaps onto agentic-sop-kit run dirs (FULL, uses the trace) or reviews any plain document (DEGRADED). Deterministic checks + a capped advisory LLM pass; the report is a DRAFT — the human owns the verdict.

plugins.name: alcoa-guard
plugins.description: Deterministic ALCOA+ data-integrity linter: checks Attributable / Contemporaneous / Complete / Accurate / Consistent in code and surfaces the human-judgment slice as a 【待補】 checklist it never auto-concludes. DEGRADED lints any CSV/JSON record against a declared contract; FULL snaps onto an agentic-sop-kit run dir. The report is a DRAFT — the human owns the verdict. Pure stdlib.

plugins.name: plugin-forge
plugins.description: Claude Code plugin linter + scaffolder: `lint` validates a plugin or whole marketplace against a house grammar (a strict superset of the manifest/frontmatter checks plus stdlib-only, hook-protocol, and test-harness invariants); `scaffold` generates a grammar-conformant plugin skeleton. Pure stdlib; self-hosting; standalone on any plugin.

environmentVariables.description: Base directory for document storage (defaults to current working directory). Ignored when BASE_DIRS is set.
environmentVariables.name: BASE_DIR

environmentVariables.description: JSON array of base directories (e.g. '["/a","/b"]'). Takes precedence over BASE_DIR.
environmentVariables.name: BASE_DIRS

environmentVariables.description: JSON array of glob patterns for files to keep out of the index, each matched against the file's path relative to its root (e.g. '["plugs/**","**/*.draft.md"]').
environmentVariables.name: IGNORE_PATHS

environmentVariables.description: Path to LanceDB database directory (defaults to ./lancedb/)
environmentVariables.name: DB_PATH

environmentVariables.description: Directory where Transformers.js models are cached (defaults to ./models/)
environmentVariables.name: CACHE_DIR

environmentVariables.description: Hugging Face model download endpoint. Set this to a mirror URL when direct downloads are blocked (defaults to https://huggingface.co).
environmentVariables.name: HF_ENDPOINT

environmentVariables.description: Embedding model name (defaults to Xenova/all-MiniLM-L6-v2)
environmentVariables.name: MODEL_NAME

environmentVariables.description: Maximum file size in bytes (defaults to 104857600 / 100MB)
environmentVariables.name: MAX_FILE_SIZE

environmentVariables.description: Maximum distance threshold for filtering search results. Results with distance greater than this value will be excluded. Lower values mean stricter filtering (e.g., 0.5 for high relevance only)
environmentVariables.name: RAG_MAX_DISTANCE

environmentVariables.description: Grouping mode for quality filtering. 'similar' returns only the most similar group (stops at first distance jump). 'related' includes related groups (stops at second distance jump). Unset means no grouping filter
environmentVariables.name: RAG_GROUPING

environmentVariables.description: Maximum number of files to keep in search results. Results are filtered to include only chunks from the top N best-scoring files. For example, 1 returns only the single best-matching file's chunks. Unset means no file filtering.
environmentVariables.name: RAG_MAX_FILES

environmentVariables.description: Minimum chunk length in characters (1-10000, defaults to 50). Chunks shorter than this threshold are filtered out during ingestion.
environmentVariables.name: CHUNK_MIN_LENGTH

environmentVariables.description: Store supported PDF and DOCX images during ingestion and return them with matched chunks (defaults to false).
environmentVariables.name: STORE_IMAGES

environmentVariables.description: Embed each chunk together with its document title, which can help when passages don't restate the topic the title names (defaults to false). After changing it, use a new DB_PATH or delete the index and re-ingest.
environmentVariables.name: EMBED_TITLE_PREFIX

environmentVariables.description: Add section headings to chunk embeddings when they fit (defaults to false). Independent of EMBED_TITLE_PREFIX. Re-ingest documents after changing it.
environmentVariables.name: EMBED_HEADING_PREFIX

environmentVariables.description: Execution device for the embedder (defaults to cpu). Passed straight to ONNX Runtime; see the Transformers.js device source for the supported backend names. If the requested device fails to initialize, the server throws an error.
environmentVariables.name: RAG_DEVICE

environmentVariables.description: Embedding quantization dtype for the embedder (defaults to fp32). Opt-in and pass-through; accepts any dtype the chosen model provides (fp32, fp16, q8, int8, ...). If the model has no variant for the requested dtype, the server throws an error. Changing this changes the embedding space — re-ingest existing data.
environmentVariables.name: RAG_DTYPE

environmentVariables.description: Keyword boost factor for hybrid search (0.0-1.0, defaults to 0.6). 0 means semantic similarity only; higher values increase the keyword-match contribution to the final score.
environmentVariables.name: RAG_HYBRID_WEIGHT

environmentVariables.description: External reranker command template. Use {query} and {top} for query text and result count; unset disables reranking.
environmentVariables.name: RAG_RERANK_CMD

environmentVariables.description: Time budget per rerank call in milliseconds (100-600000, defaults to 10000). On timeout the spawned command is killed and the pre-rerank ordering is returned.
environmentVariables.name: RAG_RERANK_TIMEOUT_MS

hooks.prompt: Apply AutoCode v6: 1) Detect the user's language, always reply in it. 2) Detect intent + project size. 3) If the user wants something like an existing product ("like X", "similar to X", names a product, pastes a product URL), run the product-study skill first: public pages only, sourced blueprint, MVP cut; the MVP hand-off is the build scope. 4) Decide what only you need to decide; ask the user ONLY when the action is costly, irreversible, or you truly don't know what they want (judge). Present decisions as 'I'll do X, ok?'. 5) I-Lang v5.0 internal planning + judgment. 6) Before any deploy, run scripts/scan-secrets.sh; if it blocks, fix the leak then ship. 7) Code without deployment = incomplete: a static build goes to GitHub Pages at no cost (ship/scripts/go_live_pages.py); rerun the acceptance against the live URL (product-study/scripts/acceptance_run.py --url) and hand back the URL, the check/expected/actual table, the actions left for the user to try, and what was learned from the studied product versus decided by you. 8) Translate errors into plain human language first; never say tests passed, show the table.

manifest.name: constraint-driven-development
manifest.description: Establishes a project's quality bar as a written contract and stops agents quietly lowering it. Interviews the user on which dimensions matter, supplies sane default thresholds when they have no number in mind, records everything in CONSTRAINTS.md, and watches the diff for a weakened bar — new @ts-ignore or eslint-disable suppressions, skipped or deleted tests, assertions stripped out, unimplemented stubs, thresholds edited down. Use when no quality bar is written down, when the user says "set up constraints" or "define our standards", when the user wants dimensions they care about — accessibility, web performance, coverage — set up as enforced constraints, when an agent keeps silencing checks or skipping tests to get to green, when you need a coverage or performance threshold and don't know what number to pick, or when an agent writes more code than anyone will read.

manifest.author: Roarpeng
manifest.overridesComment: Pinned past advisories in transitive deps. Six were non-breaking and lifted an earlier npm audit to zero: hono (cross-request data disclosure / ReDoS / SSRF-adjacent parser issues), @hono/node-server (Windows path traversal via encoded backslash), body-parser (DoS when an invalid limit silently disables size enforcement), fast-uri (host confusion and SSRF), ip-address (SSRF via octet and IPv6 misclassification), qs (array-limit bypass, DoS). @huggingface/transformers 4.3.0 pulls sharp 0.35.5 and clears the libvips/libheif CVEs; verified against the exact API surface used in src/learning/embeddings.ts (pipeline, env.cacheDir, env.remoteHost). proxy-addr ^2.0.8 clears GHSA-jqcg-44mw-7w3h (IPv4-mapped IPv6 trust spoofing) inside express, which still accepts ^2.0.7. @modelcontextprotocol/sdk is a direct dependency pinned to ^1.32.1 (advisory range was <1.31.0, GHSA-6qxp-vccf-f47h).

permissions.filesystem: read workspace sources; write graphflow-out/, .graphflow/, .graphflow-cache/ in the workspace; global config ~/.graphflow.config.json (0600)
permissions.network: LLM provider APIs listed in disclosure.network, only when a provider is configured; huggingface.co only for the first semantic-embedding model download (mirrorable via HF_ENDPOINT; embeddingProvider 'fnv' avoids it entirely); indexing/context/compression need no network
permissions.environment: read provider API keys from environment variables (disclosure.api_keys); no environment writes

plugins.name: memory-fork

plugins.name: prompt-bouncer
plugins.description: Bounces vague prompts before Claude sees them, and suggests the project's own term

plugins.name: secret-box

Installing this bundle auto-installs all four presets (v1 was removed at v2.0.0). scripts._comment:test:plugin: DSH_PROFILE_DIR= = 测试隔离铁律：本套件跑在 DSH 宿主里时环境**天然带着** DSH_PROFILE_DIR（指向真实 ~/.dsh/profiles/desktop），而多数用例只隔离了 HOME —— 于是它们会去写**真实** profile 的 cordis.patch.yml（2026-10-10 故障：测试 relayDir 被写进真 profile，面板连到假配置、验证码/公告全 502）。这里显式清空，让 profile 解析回落到各用例自己的假 HOME。 DSH_RELAY_BUNDLED_RUNTIME=/nonexistent = 强制走 npx 兜底分支（否则本机跑过 npm pack 后 packages/dsh-remote-web/runtime 存在，用例会改成走本地拷贝）。DSH_RELAY_SKIP_SERVICE=1 = 测试隔离：插件加载时不做真实系统操作（npx 补装 / launchctl / 重启 harness）；需要真实分支的用例自行 unset（见 account-switch / runtime-provision / harness-restart 用例注释）。DSH_RELAY_DEFAULT_API= 死端口：用例拆掉临时目录后，仍在飞的后台请求（装机上报重试等）会读到空配置并回落「默认云端地址」—— 指到本地死端口才不会打生产。

plugins.name: guardrails
plugins.description: Safety guardrails for running Claude Code with reduced supervision. The guard-destructive PreToolUse hook matches against a normalized view of each command (heredoc bodies and comments stripped, quoted strings neutralized except interpreter arguments like ssh / sh -c / eval / su / doas), so a command that merely mentions a destructive pattern is not flagged. It hard-blocks catastrophic Bash commands (rm -rf /, rsync --delete, docker volume rm) and makes rm/rmdir scope-aware: operations whose operands all resolve inside the allowed workspace (the session project root, temp dirs, any $GUARD_ALLOWED_EXTRA root, or a variable assigned from a bare mktemp earlier in the same command) run silently, while anything outside it (or any glob/variable/escape it cannot resolve) raises a single reflective confirmation. git reset --hard / clean / restore, shred, dd, mkfs still always prompt.

plugins.name: privacy-guard
plugins.description: Keeps private infrastructure details out of public repositories. Ships the privacy-guard skill: session rules for what must never cross the public boundary, plus a per-repo pre-commit gate built on a gitignored local denylist and gitleaks. The denylist is never committed, so the hook is a no-op for external contributors and in CI while gitleaks still covers generic secrets.

plugins.name: decision-records
plugins.description: Creates, supersedes and validates decision records (ADRs) against the convention a collection already follows, instead of against a published spec it may never have adopted. Ships the decision-records skill: a propose-then-write flow that never rewrites an accepted record, and check-decisions.sh, a validator that deduces the filename scheme, section set and status vocabulary from the records already present and reports eight classes of violation with a stable code and an exit status. Ships no template into the target repo, and delegates private-token scanning to privacy-guard rather than keeping a second denylist.

name: libre-embed
description: 15 Claude Code plugins for embedded systems, firmware, and IoT development

metadata.description: Embedded systems, firmware, and IoT plugins for Claude Code, from bare metal to RTOS.

plugins.name: arm-cortex-m
plugins.description: ARM Cortex-M core programming across M0 to M33: CMSIS, startup code, NVIC, SysTick, FPU, MPU, and sleep modes.

plugins.name: bare-metal
plugins.description: Bare-metal firmware without a HAL: register-level drivers, linker scripts, startup code, and minimal runtimes.

plugins.name: bootloader-design
plugins.description: MCU bootloader architecture: flash layouts, image verification, signature checks, secure boot, and fail-safe recovery.

plugins.name: communication-buses
plugins.description: I2C, SPI, UART, CAN, and USB drivers with DMA strategy, error recovery, bit timing math, and MCU peripheral quirks.

plugins.name: debug-trace
plugins.description: On-target debugging for Cortex-M: SWD and JTAG probes, HardFault decoding, GDB, ITM and SWO trace, and DWT timing.

plugins.name: embedded-linux
plugins.description: Embedded Linux on ARM SoCs: Yocto, Buildroot, device trees, kernel modules, cross-compilation, and U-Boot.

plugins.name: embedded-testing
plugins.description: Firmware testing: Unity, CMock, and Ceedling unit tests, hardware mocks, QEMU, hardware-in-the-loop, and coverage.

plugins.name: firmware-update
plugins.description: Firmware over-the-air updates: dual-bank flash, MCUboot, ESP-IDF OTA, delta images, version checks, and automatic rollback.

plugins.name: fpga-integration
plugins.description: MCU and FPGA integration: Verilog register interfaces, AXI-Lite and SPI links, timing constraints, and MCU drivers.

plugins.name: iot-protocols
plugins.description: IoT connectivity: choosing between MQTT, CoAP, LwM2M, BLE, LoRaWAN, Thread, and Zigbee, then designing the protocol layer.

plugins.name: memory-management
plugins.description: Deterministic firmware memory: static allocation, memory pools, FreeRTOS heaps, stack sizing, and MPU protection.

plugins.name: power-management
plugins.description: Low-power firmware: sleep modes, tickless idle, clock gating, wake sources, current measurement, and battery life budgets.

plugins.name: rtos-patterns
plugins.description: FreeRTOS and Zephyr firmware design: task graphs, IPC sizing, priority inversion, watchdogs, and stack sizing.

plugins.name: safety-critical
plugins.description: Safety-critical firmware: MISRA C, IEC 61508, ISO 26262, DO-178C, defensive coding, watchdogs, and static analysis.

plugins.name: sensor-integration
plugins.description: Sensor integration: drivers from datasheets, calibration, digital filtering, Kalman filters, and IMU sensor fusion.

plugins.name: libre-embed-hooks
plugins.description: Optional safety hooks for firmware work: confirm before flash, erase, and secret-file operations, detect embedded projects at session start, and flag empty files after edits.

The `/diagnose` command surfaces the mutually-corrected models on demand as a readable report. The `ConceptualPipelineMap` template adds a standalone, presentation-agnostic flow-perspective data model; the agent's `scope-resolution` mode answers 'what does my task touch?' (a bounded, disclosed scope from a work task); and its `pipeline` mode traces control flow within that bound into a ConceptualPipelineMap alongside the architectural/domain collections, then cross-checks all three against each other (the maximal six directed pairs) for mutual correction. The `/pipeline-map "<task>"` command renders the task-scoped map as a self-contained HTML flowchart (pinned, SHA-verified Mermaid inlined; no CDN) with a scope-resolution panel, node-detail table, and no-JS fallback; `--predict-change` adds an opt-in change-site prediction (which stages the task will modify and where it will insert new ones) disclosed as a prediction, never a directive.

environmentVariables.description: TLS mode. require/allow/prefer encrypt without verifying the certificate; verify-ca/verify-full verify it (supply a CA via PG_SSL_CA). Unlike libpq, allow/prefer do not fall back to plaintext, so a server without TLS needs disable.

io.modelcontextprotocol.registry/publish.endpoint_probe: POST tools/list on https://analyticslegends.ai/mcp -> 200, 22 tools (2026-10-11), protocol 2025-11-25, 3 resources, 4 prompts. Paid conformance 2026-08-18 on the deployed fingerprint: 686 assertions, 0 failed.
io.modelcontextprotocol.registry/publish.long_description: Source-backed intelligence on the SAP AI & analytics services market (Joule, BDC, Datasphere, SAC, BW/4HANA, Databricks), read-only, so an assistant can answer precisely and cite the exact record. TWENTY-TWO tools: FOURTEEN public and unauthenticated, plus EIGHT a subscriber key opens (listed, refusing by name, never hidden): a directory of SAP consulting, recruitment and vendor organisations searchable by country and kind, a profile per firm, and an aggregate count for an agent that needs a number, not a page of rows; a published day-rate aggregate by geography, stack and seniority — small, all secondary sources, sample_size null where no observation matches the cell, GBP/CHF never folded into euro rows; a live contract radar of publicly published SAP analytics openings, each with its own page — filter it by employment_type, because it is mostly PERMANENT roles and an unfiltered page answers a contracting question with salaried jobs; many rows carry a panel-inferred P25-P75 day-rate band for their seniority x product x region cell, served with its basis, sample and source so it is never quotable as the employer's own offer; what is gated there is a FIELD, not a row: the verified link to the original listing is the Consultant deliverable, every other fact and the page stay public; a curated market-news corpus de-duplicated by upstream URL, its size read at query time and returned as _meta.match_count, each item carrying the upstream publisher's URL alongside ours; a concept encyclopaedia of the stack's vocabulary; the SAP module lookup; and the metadata of the deep-research studies on market structure, day rates and recruiter economics — each exists in EN and FR, so rows are EDITIONS. Also public: the CV/profile platforms a consultant can sign up on, the Academy catalogue, and a traversal of the learning knowledge graph. Every tool is annotated readOnlyHint. The fourteen public tools need no credential; the eight paid ones need an analyticslegends.ai subscription (Consultant or above) or the MCP Pass (€39.90/month, analyticslegends.ai/pricing) — three open at Consultant (the full concept card, a study body, an Academy module) and five at Legend (firm intelligence, the SAP end-customer corpus and profiles, expansion brief, partner candidates). A key on a FREE account gets a small daily taste of the paid tranche (the number is in analytics-legends://tranche). Retrieval with attribution is permitted, training is not; every response carries a citation_url. DELIBERATELY NOT SERVED at any tier: the opportunity-to-consultant matchers, and people — consultants are held as initials only; no tool returns anyone's identity or contact details.
io.modelcontextprotocol.registry/publish.monitoring: Handshake, a real tools/call with data, and latency. Two watchers: a 20-minute tick on the maintainer's workstation (only while awake), and a cloud backstop twice a day calling tools/list AND a data-returning tools/call (added 2026-08-18; before that it watched the website only). Health: https://analyticslegends.ai/api/mcp-health.json — read its generated_at, do not assume a cadence.
io.modelcontextprotocol.registry/publish.repository_scope: This repository is the server's PUBLIC FACE — manifest, descriptor, client config, docs. It carries no server code (the application repository is private: paid corpus, personal data). tools/list against the endpoint is the authority for the surface.
io.modelcontextprotocol.registry/publish.tools_served: 22 on this endpoint: 14 public and unauthenticated, 8 gated by tier and refused by name (3 at Consultant, 5 at Legend). The MCP Pass opens all eight.
io.modelcontextprotocol.registry/publish.transport_path: Cloudflare Worker on analyticslegends.ai/mcp* -> Supabase Edge Function -> Postgres

metadata.description: Embedded systems, firmware, and IoT plugins for Claude Code, from bare metal to RTOS.

plugins.name: arm-cortex-m
plugins.description: ARM Cortex-M core programming across M0 to M33: CMSIS, startup code, NVIC, SysTick, FPU, MPU, and sleep modes.

plugins.name: bare-metal
plugins.description: Bare-metal firmware without a HAL: register-level drivers, linker scripts, startup code, and minimal runtimes.

plugins.name: bootloader-design
plugins.description: MCU bootloader architecture: flash layouts, image verification, signature checks, secure boot, and fail-safe recovery.

plugins.name: communication-buses
plugins.description: I2C, SPI, UART, CAN, and USB drivers with DMA strategy, error recovery, bit timing math, and MCU peripheral quirks.

plugins.name: debug-trace
plugins.description: On-target debugging for Cortex-M: SWD and JTAG probes, HardFault decoding, GDB, ITM and SWO trace, and DWT timing.

plugins.name: embedded-linux
plugins.description: Embedded Linux on ARM SoCs: Yocto, Buildroot, device trees, kernel modules, cross-compilation, and U-Boot.

plugins.name: embedded-testing
plugins.description: Firmware testing: Unity, CMock, and Ceedling unit tests, hardware mocks, QEMU, hardware-in-the-loop, and coverage.

plugins.name: firmware-update
plugins.description: Firmware over-the-air updates: dual-bank flash, MCUboot, ESP-IDF OTA, delta images, version checks, and automatic rollback.

plugins.name: fpga-integration
plugins.description: MCU and FPGA integration: Verilog register interfaces, AXI-Lite and SPI links, timing constraints, and MCU drivers.

plugins.name: iot-protocols
plugins.description: IoT connectivity: choosing between MQTT, CoAP, LwM2M, BLE, LoRaWAN, Thread, and Zigbee, then designing the protocol layer.

plugins.name: memory-management
plugins.description: Deterministic firmware memory: static allocation, memory pools, FreeRTOS heaps, stack sizing, and MPU protection.

plugins.name: power-management
plugins.description: Low-power firmware: sleep modes, tickless idle, clock gating, wake sources, current measurement, and battery life budgets.

plugins.name: rtos-patterns
plugins.description: FreeRTOS and Zephyr firmware design: task graphs, IPC sizing, priority inversion, watchdogs, and stack sizing.

plugins.name: safety-critical
plugins.description: Safety-critical firmware: MISRA C, IEC 61508, ISO 26262, DO-178C, defensive coding, watchdogs, and static analysis.

plugins.name: sensor-integration
plugins.description: Sensor integration: drivers from datasheets, calibration, digital filtering, Kalman filters, and IMU sensor fusion.

plugins.name: libre-embed-hooks
plugins.description: Optional safety hooks for firmware work: confirm before flash, erase, and secret-file operations, detect embedded projects at session start, and flag empty files after edits.

manifest.name: modern-web-guidance
manifest.description: Search tool for modern web development best practices. MANDATORY: Execute FIRST for all HTML/CSS and clientside JS tasks. Do NOT skip — web APIs evolve rapidly and training weights contain obsolete patterns. Trigger immediately for: - UI/Layout: Modals/dialogs/popovers, tables, dark mode, anchor positioning, container queries, `:has()`, etc. - Scroll/Motion: View Transitions, Scroll-driven animations, parallax/reveals, etc. - Performance: CWV (LCP, INP), content-visibility, Fetch Priority, image optimization, etc. - System/APIs: Security, passkeys, HTML sanitization, Web Components, dates/timezones, Built-in AI, WebAssembly, etc. - Frameworks: Standard HTML/CSS/DOM in React, Vue, Angular, etc. - General Frontend: Forms, validation (`:user-valid`), autofill, accessibility, custom selects, scrollbars, etc. DO NOT trigger for: - Backend: SQL, ORMs, API routes, etc. - Infra/Scripts: CI/CD, Docker, Actions, Python/Go, Git, etc. - Tooling/Trivial: Vite, tsconfig, ESLint, tests, copy/renames, 3P docs, etc.

environmentVariables.name: DATABASE_URL
environmentVariables.description: Your own PostgreSQL, where this library keeps file ownership, grants and the audit chain. Apply node_modules/@filelayer/core/schema.sql once before starting.

environmentVariables.name: FILELAYER_AS
environmentVariables.description: The ONE subject this server speaks for, in your own id space. Fixed for the life of the process: no tool reads it as an argument and no tool can change it, which is the only reason exposing these tools to an agent is safe. Write it yourself or have your provisioning write it, never derive it from a conversation. Serving several people means starting several servers.

environmentVariables.name: FILELAYER_ORG
environmentVariables.description: The organisation this server is scoped to, in your own id space.

environmentVariables.name: FILELAYER_DATA_DIR
environmentVariables.description: A local directory for the bytes. Needs no bucket and no IAM user. Set this OR the S3_* block: with neither, the server refuses to start rather than falling back to memory, which would work in a demo and lose the first real file.

environmentVariables.name: S3_ENDPOINT
environmentVariables.description: An S3-compatible endpoint, for example https://<account>.r2.cloudflarestorage.com. Setting it makes S3_BUCKET, S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID and S3_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY required.

environmentVariables.name: S3_BUCKET
environmentVariables.description: The bucket. It must be private: this library decides who may be GIVEN a URL and has no say in who the object store will answer. `npx -p @filelayer/core filelayer doctor` reports whether yours serves unauthenticated reads.

environmentVariables.name: S3_REGION
environmentVariables.description: Region, or `auto` for Cloudflare R2.

environmentVariables.name: S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID
environmentVariables.description: Access key id for the bucket.

environmentVariables.name: S3_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY
environmentVariables.description: Secret access key for the bucket.

environmentVariables.name: FILELAYER_MCP_AGENT_LABEL
environmentVariables.description: How this agent names itself in the audit trail, recorded on every event these tools produce. It is what lets the chain separate "the partner opened this document" from "the partner's assistant opened this document".

environmentVariables.name: FILELAYER_MCP_ALLOW_DESTRUCTIVE
environmentVariables.description: Set to exactly `true` to register delete_file. Off by default because deleting is not recoverable and an agent that misreads a sentence deletes the wrong thing silently.

environmentVariables.name: FILELAYER_MCP_EXPOSE_AUDIT
environmentVariables.description: Set to exactly `true` to register file_audit. Off by default because the trail is an organisation's whole history and a tool that returns it copies every file name, actor and denial into the model's context. Reading it is itself audited since 0.27.0, which was the previous reason; the default did not move.

environmentVariables.name: FILELAYER_MCP_RETURN_BYTES
environmentVariables.description: Set to exactly `true` to register read_file. Off by default because a document returned by a tool is a document copied into a model's context; file_info plus a share link is usually what was actually needed.

environmentVariables.name: FILELAYER_BASE_URL
environmentVariables.description: The base of the share URLs this instance mints. Without it, share links come back without a URL.

typesafe_api_key.title: TypeSafe API key
typesafe_api_key.description: Key for the Jev API. Leave empty to use the TYPESAFE_API_KEY environment variable.

python.title: Python executable
python.description: Python 3.10+ used to run the tools, e.g. python, python3 or a full path. Empty means python.

jev_dashboard_mode.title: Dashboard
jev_dashboard_mode.description: on: show live compacter, router and skill-picker status above the prompt. off: use the compact status line instead.

jev_compacter_mode.title: Compaction: Jev
jev_compacter_mode.description: on: /compact and auto-compaction prune stale tool calls with Jev, keeping everything else verbatim. off: Claude Code's built-in summary.

jev_compacter_soft_percent.title: Compaction: soft threshold (%)
jev_compacter_soft_percent.description: Context fill at which Jev pruning is tried after a turn. Empty means 60.

jev_compacter_hard_percent.title: Compaction: hard threshold (%)
jev_compacter_hard_percent.description: Context fill at which compaction must shrink, falling back to the built-in summary. Empty means 85.

jev_compacter_target_percent.title: Compaction: target (%)
jev_compacter_target_percent.description: A pruning that lands at or below this fill is always applied. Empty means 40.

jev_compacter_min_freed_tokens.title: Compaction: minimum tokens freed
jev_compacter_min_freed_tokens.description: Above the target, a pruning is applied only if it frees at least this many tokens. Empty means 8000.

jev_compacter_keep_threshold.title: Compaction: keep threshold
jev_compacter_keep_threshold.description: Minimum Jev probability for a tool call or its output to stay. Empty means 0.5.

jev_compacter_preserve_recent_messages.title: Compaction: recent messages kept
jev_compacter_preserve_recent_messages.description: Newest messages never touched. Empty means 6.

jev_skills_mode.title: Skills: Jev picker
jev_skills_mode.description: on: the built-in list of every skill is left out; Jev shortlists the skills each prompt needs. /jev-skills on|off changes it per session.

jev_skills_scope.title: Skills: scope
jev_skills_scope.description: project: .claude/skills in this project. global: also ~/.claude/skills and installed plugins' skills, whose folders Claude may then read without asking.

jev_skills_max_picks.title: Skills: shortlist size
jev_skills_max_picks.description: Most skills shortlisted for one prompt. Empty means 3.

jev_skills_min_percent.title: Skills: shortlist bar (%)
jev_skills_min_percent.description: Jev's share a skill needs to be shortlisted (it must also beat 'none'). Empty means 30.

jev_skills_max_input_tokens.title: Skills: Jev input cap (tokens)
jev_skills_max_input_tokens.description: Most tokens sent to Jev in one shortlist request; earlier prompts are trimmed first, then skills are split into smaller batches. Empty means 3000.

jev_router_mode.title: Router: default mode
jev_router_mode.description: on: the main model changes files only through subagents, and Jev picks each subagent's model. /jev-route on|off changes it per session.

jev_router_cap.title: Router: cap at the session model
jev_router_cap.description: on: Jev never picks a subagent model above the session's (rules and escalation still can).

jev_router_escalate_after.title: Router: errors before escalating
jev_router_escalate_after.description: Failed edits in one subagent after which the next subagent for its files starts a model up. Empty means 3.

jev_router_max_input_tokens.title: Router: Jev input cap (tokens)
jev_router_max_input_tokens.description: Most tokens sent to Jev for one routing decision; context is trimmed lowest-priority first. Still over: the decider model below picks instead. Empty means 4000.

jev_router_decider_model.title: Router: decider when Jev's input is too large
jev_router_decider_model.description: Claude model that picks a subagent's model and effort when Jev's input stays over the cap after trimming. Empty means haiku.

jev_router_init_model.title: Router: rules writer model
jev_router_init_model.description: Model that drafts rules.json during /jev-route init. Empty means sonnet.

name: skills
description: 23 practical agent skills: TeamWorkflow, multi-model review, media ingestion, and writing. Original Claude Code packages plus a Codex desktop edition tuned for Astra. Source for clickai.dev.

metadata.description: Portable skills for AI agents: a multi-model advisory board for hard decisions, a seventeen-skill team-workflow pack for tracked, multi-session, agent-assisted development, a media-ingest skill that turns recordings and URLs into evidence, a pair of writing references — one for documents agents consume, one for pages humans read — and a plain-language decoder for agent messages that didn't land.

plugins.name: advisory-board
plugins.description: Convene a board of frontier AI models — Claude, Codex, Gemini, and Grok — that each review the same decision independently, debate across rounds, and hand back one clear recommendation.

plugins.name: team-workflow
plugins.description: Seventeen skills that ship as one pack — a portable discipline for tracked, multi-session, agent-assisted development: the orchestrator seat a non-engineer works from (one session routing, auditing, and merging parallel lanes), a router entry point, a once-per-repo setup interview that records whether you lead from that seat or read code and pick skills, per-repo institutional memory written as side effects of work, relentless grilling, decision maps, throwaway prototypes, autonomous research lanes, ticket filing, human-step wizards, session handoffs, a build discipline of seam-scoped test-first tracer slices, a disciplined bug-diagnosis loop where no fix ships without a named cause, an adversarial review that breaks changes before they ship, a skeptic-verified state review of the codebase itself, an append-only decision trail that lets a human audit an unattended run after stepping away, and a PR-writing standard that leads with the problem, shows before-and-after proof, and says whether a revert undoes the change. Versioned together (team-workflow/vX.Y.Z); this version mirrors the latest pack tag.

plugins.name: ingest
plugins.description: Turn a video, recording, voice memo, or media URL into an evidence packet — authoritative whisper transcript, timestamped frames, manifest — plus a routing recommendation. Six intents behind a mandatory purpose gate; the pipeline script is resumable and encodes the hard-won gotchas.

plugins.name: huh
plugins.description: Decode an agent message that didn't land — a plain-sentence restatement, every piece of invented shorthand expanded, what's being asked of you separated from what happened, and unevidenced claims flagged.

plugins.name: writing-for-agents
plugins.description: Write and prune documents an agent consumes — a SKILL.md, an AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md, a reference reached by a pointer. Context pointers, the two loads, the information hierarchy, leading words, and the no-op test.

plugins.name: writing-for-humans
plugins.description: Write copy a human reads — a landing page, a README's front half, a launch post. Guide structure over catalog structure, the warmth moves, three named failure modes, standing voice rules, and a last-mile AI-tell scrub.

plugins.name: plainspoken
plugins.description: Write like a person in everything the agent emits: plain words, concrete claims, no AI tells. Always on for chat replies, status updates, close-outs, review comments, and commit messages; owns the repo's single merged tell catalog behind a pointer.

plugins.name: blast-radius
plugins.description: Find what a change breaks somewhere else before it ships: past where grep stops, risks graded with real file:line cites, and the one fact the change is safe because of proven by running real code.

Escalating repeat detection for dsh: a synchronous ctx.tools.guard gate that counts semantic fingerprints (exact/cmd/net/host/sink) over a per-agent sliding window, warns at 7, demands a progress summary at 11, and gates at 12 (16 for the coarser host: measure), plus a second track on consecutive failures (advisory at 3, block at 5) — asking the operator for a turn-scoped exemption instead of only blocking. scripts.//check: Build runs BEFORE typecheck on purpose. Each adapter resolves the core through the `jevcore` workspace link, and the core's `types` entry is `lib/index.d.ts` — which does not exist until it is built. Typechecking first works on any machine that already has a `lib/` and fails on a clean checkout, which is exactly how CI caught it.
scripts.//check:workflows: Runs before build, beside the other gates that read committed text rather than build output. It exists because the trap it catches fired twice in this repository: bash performs command substitution on backticks inside a `run:` block before the program in that block sees the text, so a backtick written in a JavaScript comment inside `node -e "..."` is executed as a shell command. The first occurrence was diagnosed and documented in a NOTE; the second was added by the change that wrote this gate.
scripts.//check:docs: Runs BEFORE build, and reads no build output: it compares docs/ with the copies in packages/*/docs, both of which are committed. The placement is about repairs, which is what separates it from check:mojibake below. That gate's drift half has to run after the build because only a build clears a stale artifact, so running it earlier printed the same advisories on every un-rebuilt tree. Nothing in this chain clears a stale copy — `build` compiles TypeScript and never reads `docs/`, so a copy that is behind stays behind until someone runs the sync. Failing before a build that cannot help is therefore the cheap order, and it sits beside `legal` because it is the same kind of gate: a generated directory that `files[]` ships, asserted by its own `--check` mode and repaired by running its script.
scripts.//check:mojibake: Runs AFTER build, not before. Before it, every un-rebuilt edit made the chain print the same stale-artifact advisories; noise on the normal path is how a real finding gets skimmed past, and nothing ships on that path anyway — release.yml runs this whole chain, build included, before it publishes. After it, the corruption half scans the artifact the build just produced, and the drift half stays quiet unless a rebuild could not have fixed what it found.
scripts.check: pnpm run legal && pnpm run check:docs && pnpm run check:readmes && pnpm run check:workflows && pnpm run build && pnpm run check:mojibake && pnpm run typecheck && pnpm run test

manifest.//files: 根包打包边界（v1.4.7 收面批）：private:true 只拦得住 npm publish，拦不住 npm pack / --dry-run。此前既无 files 也无 .npmignore → npm 回退用 .gitignore 排除 → 排除不到 → 实测打过 1621 文件 / 17.3 MB 解包，平铺含 FORGE/ docs/ engine/ tools/ SKILL/ FDE/ .claude/ .cursor/（把内部施工面连同一份含凭证路径说明的配置一起打进 tarball）。本字段把根 pack 收敛到根级必要文件。⚠️ 不影响 @sofagent/* 各 workspace 包（各自 files 独立限定，如 engine/umbrella 恒为 3 文件）；也不影响 install.sh（走 git clone 钉发版 tag，不走 npm pack）。⚠️ 维护注意：根 pack 只用于边界收口，无任何发布/安装链路依赖它——新增根级文件如确需随包分发再显式登记。
manifest.//build-scope: 根 build 覆盖边界（v1.5.1 K4 显式声明，非缺陷）：scripts.build 按拓扑序显式枚举 22 个子命令 = 22 个 workspace 包（其中 engine/dsh-plugins/plugin-kit 以 `npm --prefix` 形态调用而非 --workspace，故仍先于全部 DSH 插件构建——构建拓扑序由本字段手工钉住）。27 项 workspaces 中未被根 build 覆盖的 5 项为：engine/umbrella（无 build 脚本——纯转发壳，bin/sofagent.js 是源码级入口，合理）+ 4 个 engine/openclaw-plugins/sofagent-{audit,evolve,inject,rollback}。⚠️ 后 4 个**各自带 build 脚本但刻意不随根 build 构建**——它们走 OpenClaw 独立分发通道（ClawHub），产物面与根 monorepo 的 npm 发布面相互独立；install.sh 亦不消费其 dist（故当前无故障，属显式声明的潜伏断链收口）。ClawHub 通道构建验证点（v1.5.8 BUG-31 登记）：发版前由维护者在本地对 4 包各跑 `npm --prefix engine/openclaw-plugins/<pkg> run build` 确认零报错 + dist 时间戳更新，随发版阶段九（双分发）取证记录在 devlog（`clawhub build ok ×4` 一行）；ClawHub 上架后的可用性以平台安装回验为准。如需改为纳入根 build、或在文档中另作声明，须先确认分发形态。

manifest.//postbuild: chmod 覆盖面说明（v1.4.7 批次 J-5 核对）：hooks/sofagent-load-chain 与 umbrella 两包不在 dirs 列表——hooks 无 bin 入口（handler.js 是 require 消费不需可执行位）；umbrella 的 bin/sofagent.js 是源码级入口非 dist 产物，git 已带 755 可执行位（100755，npm 安装保留 git mode），不经 postbuild。

`jelou workflow validate` flags a read of an AI node's output when the node declares no output fields. Before, a condition on it always took the `else` branch.
The warning for a plain HTTP node that hardcodes a Datum key now names the header and asks you to rotate the key and use a secret instead.
The AI node spec bundled with the skills now includes a Databases v2 section with a pinned example.

manifest.description: Read, send, file and search email in any Gmail, Microsoft 365 or IMAP mailbox, plus its calendar.
manifest.title: Mailbox MCP

com.mailbox-mcp.authentication: OAuth 2.1 with dynamic client registration and PKCE. Mailbox credentials are envelope-encrypted and are never held by the client.
com.mailbox-mcp.summary: Mailbox MCP connects an assistant to a real mailbox over IMAP and SMTP, so it can read, write, file and search mail as the owner would. The mailbox has to look untouched afterwards in Outlook or webmail, and that rule decides the implementation: reading never marks a message as read, a send files exactly one copy in Sent, a delete moves to Trash, a draft is saved where another client can edit it, a move keeps flags and the internal date, and folders resolve by their special-use flag instead of by name. It archives and reports spam by role rather than by folder name, so on Gmail archiving drops the inbox label. It reads attachments: a PDF, a Word file or a spreadsheet as text, a photo as a picture. After a send, check_bounces says whether an address failed for good or is being retried, and check_receipts whether it was opened, even when nothing came back. catch_up, waiting_on and owed_replies answer in one call each what came in, what nobody has answered and who is waiting on a reply. A diary connected as a separate step adds calendar tools: reading and searching events, free/busy, booking and moving your own time, inviting, cancelling, answering or proposing another time, and the out-of-office reply. A CardDAV address book connected to an IMAP mailbox, also separately, lets find_contact read the book beside the mailbox's own history, and adds read_contact to open one card. No contact is stored on the server. A mailbox with no diary or book is handed none of those tools rather than tools that refuse, so the tool count varies by mailbox.
com.mailbox-mcp.toolsNote: This list is the mail surface, which every connected mailbox gets. The calendar and contact tools are absent: each is registered only on a mailbox whose owner has connected a diary or an address book, and Outlook contacts on a Microsoft mailbox that reconnects, so listing them here would be a promise the server had not kept. find_contact is on every mailbox; a connected book improves it. The summary says what each adds.

Gmail and Google Workspace, with an app password
Microsoft 365 and Google calendars, over OAuth

manifest.title: HAPI MCP Server

headers.description: Authorization token for accessing the MCP server
headers.name: Authorization

runtimeArguments.description: Port mapping for the host to container (e.g., '3030:3030'). Adjust second port if changing internal container port (HAPI_PORT)
runtimeArguments.name: -p

runtimeArguments.description: Volume mapping for HAPI configuration directory
runtimeArguments.name: -v

packageArguments.description: Command to start the HAPI MCP server
packageArguments.name: serve

packageArguments.description: The name of the project/API to serve (e.g., 'petstore'). Optional when using HAPI_OPENAPI environment variable
packageArguments.name: projectName

packageArguments.description: The port to listen on inside the container
packageArguments.name: --port

packageArguments.description: Run in headless mode (serve MCP-only, no business logic)
packageArguments.name: --headless

packageArguments.description: The server provides REST API's business logic AND also exposes them as MCP tools
packageArguments.name: --mcp

packageArguments.description: Enable development mode with verbose logging
packageArguments.name: --dev

packageArguments.description: The full URL for the backend API server (overrides OpenAPI spec servers). Uses OAS server URL if not provided
packageArguments.name: --url

packageArguments.description: OpenAPI spec file path or URL to use instead of loading from HAPI_HOME
packageArguments.name: --openapi

packageArguments.description: Comma-separated list of allowed origins for CORS (e.g., 'http://localhost:3000,https://example.com')
packageArguments.name: --cors

packageArguments.description: Comma-separated list of OAS configuration files to apply (can be URLs)
packageArguments.name: --filename

packageArguments.description: Path to SSL certificate file for HTTPS. Volume mount required if using Docker. https://docs.mcp.com.ai/components/hapi-server/hapi-cli#running-with-tls-https
packageArguments.name: --cert

packageArguments.description: Path to SSL key file for HTTPS. Volume mount required if using Docker
packageArguments.name: --key

environmentVariables.description: Fully Qualified Domain Name for the HAPI server (used in MCP tool URLs)
environmentVariables.name: HAPI_FQDN

environmentVariables.description: Directory path for HAPI configuration and specs. Should be mounted as a volume in Docker
environmentVariables.name: HAPI_HOME

environmentVariables.description: The name of the project/API (alternative to positional argument)
environmentVariables.name: PROJECT_NAME

environmentVariables.description: OpenAPI spec URL or path (alternative to --openapi flag)
environmentVariables.name: HAPI_OPENAPI

environmentVariables.description: Backend API base URL (alternative to --url flag)
environmentVariables.name: HAPI_URL

environmentVariables.description: Server port (alternative to --port flag) - this is the internal container port
environmentVariables.name: HAPI_PORT

environmentVariables.description: Enable headless mode (alternative to --headless flag)
environmentVariables.name: HAPI_HEADLESS

environmentVariables.description: Enable MCP mode (alternative to --mcp flag)
environmentVariables.name: HAPI_MCP

environmentVariables.description: Enable development mode (alternative to --dev flag)
environmentVariables.name: HAPI_DEV

environmentVariables.description: Comma-separated allowed CORS origins (alternative to --cors flag)
environmentVariables.name: HAPI_CORS

environmentVariables.description: Comma-separated configuration files (alternative to --filename flag)
environmentVariables.name: HAPI_CONFIG_FILES

environmentVariables.description: Node environment (development, production). 'development' enables verbose logging and debugging features.
environmentVariables.name: NODE_ENV

HAPI_FQDN.description: Fully Qualified Domain Name for the HAPI server
